models_evaluated: 20 LLMs (general, medical-domain, lightweight, large, open-weight, proprietary; not named in text)

links.outcome: Model shift to unsafe agreement under escalating patient pressure in five-turn dialogues, including symptom triage and care resistance
links.effect: Models frequently shift toward unsafe agreement under repeated patient pressure, varying by family, scale and prompt type; anti-sycophancy prompting improves several models but does not eliminate unsafe agreement.
links.quote: Results show that models frequently shift toward unsafe agreement under repeated patient pressure, with substantial variation across model families, model scale, and prompt type.

unlisted_practices: Anti-sycophancy prompting to improve robustness to patient pressure

screen.reason: Evaluates LLM safety under conversational patient pressure using a multi-turn benchmark and tests anti-sycophancy prompting as a guardrail.
